module.purpose: This client-side utility module provides reusable React hooks and compatibility helpers for stable callbacks, previous-value tracking, DOM intersection observation, forwarded refs, and React version-safe behavior.
module.summary: The file centralizes small React utilities used by components that need stable callback identities, change detection across renders, browser intersection observation, and forwarded DOM refs. It also dynamically accesses the newer React use capability to remain compatible with React 18 bundlers, and selects a server-safe layout effect implementation.
module.businessContext: These utilities support reliable interactive React interfaces across server-rendered and browser environments. Failures can cause hydration warnings, stale callbacks, broken visibility-driven behavior, or incorrect DOM ref handling.
functions: useStableCallback (~L20-28): Maintains a stable callback identity while invoking the latest function.
usePrevious (~L38-58): Tracks and returns the prior value across React renders.
useIntersectionObserver (~L82-110): Observes an element and reports intersection changes through a callback.
useForwardedRef (~L126-130): Converts a forwarded ref into an internally usable mutable ref.

io: Creates an IntersectionObserver and observes the supplied DOM element when enabled.

units.name: useStableCallback

detail.name: useStableCallback
detail.signature: export function useStableCallback<T extends (...args: Array<any>) => any>(fn: T): T
preconditions: fn is callable and satisfies the generic function type T.
The function is invoked within a valid React hook execution context.
postconditions: Returns a function assignable to T.
The returned function identity remains stable across rerenders of the same component instance.
Calling the returned function delegates to the latest supplied fn with the original arguments and preserves its return value.
invariants: The returned callback reference is initialized once per component instance.
The callback dispatch target is updated to the latest fn on each render.
edgeCases: When called with different fn references across rerenders, the returned callback reference remains unchanged and later calls use the newest fn.
When called with no arguments or multiple arguments, all arguments are forwarded unchanged.
If the delegated fn throws, that exception propagates to the caller.

raises: Any exception thrown by the delegated fn is propagated unchanged.
errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: The fn argument must be callable; invalid runtime input is not otherwise normalized.

stateMutations: Mutates the internal React ref holding the latest fn by assigning fnRef.current on each render.
detail.summary: Returns a callback with stable identity across renders while ensuring invocations delegate to the most recently supplied function.

specTests.when: The callback returned from the first render is invoked after the rerender.
specTests.then: The same callback reference is retained and fn2 receives the invocation arguments.

specTests.when: The stable callback is invoked with zero or more arguments.
specTests.then: The arguments are forwarded in the same order and the delegated return value is returned unchanged.
The same exception is thrown to the caller.

units.name: usePrevious

detail.name: usePrevious
detail.signature: export function usePrevious<T>(value: T): T | null
preconditions: The function is invoked in a valid React hook context.
A value of type T is provided.
postconditions: Returns null on the first invocation for a hook instance.
Returns the immediately preceding stored value when the current value differs from the stored value by strict inequality.
Returns the previously stored previous value when the current value is strictly equal to the stored current value.
invariants: The hook retains its ref-backed state across renders for the same hook instance.
The stored current value is updated only when the supplied value is not strictly equal to the stored current value.
The returned value is the stored previous value, never the current input value.
edgeCases: Initial invocation returns null because no previous value exists.
Repeated strictly equal primitive values do not advance the previous value.
Distinct object or function references are treated as changed even when their contents or behavior are equivalent.
NaN is treated as changed on each comparison because the comparison uses strict inequality.
stateMutations: Mutates the React ref state for the hook instance by replacing its stored current and previous values when the input changes.
detail.summary: Maintains the previously observed value across hook renders and returns it. On the initial render, or before any value change, it returns null.

specTests.then: The result is 10, and subsequent rendering with value 20 continues to return 10.

specTests.when: It is rendered again with the strictly equal value 10.
specTests.then: The result remains null because no changed value has established a previous value.

detail.name: useIntersectionObserver
preconditions: ref is a React.RefObject whose current value is either an Element compatible with T or null.
postconditions: When observation is enabled and IntersectionObserver is available, an observer is registered for ref.current.
The observer callback receives the last entry from each delivered entries array, or undefined when the array is empty.
Effect cleanup disconnects the observer when one was created and invokes callback with undefined.
invariants: Observation uses a root margin of exactly 100px.
Cleanup invokes callback without an entry.
If observation is skipped, the returned cleanup still invokes callback without an entry.
edgeCases: When ref.current is null, no observer is created or observed, and cleanup invokes callback with undefined.
When disabled is true, no observer is created or observed, and cleanup invokes callback with undefined.
When IntersectionObserver is not a function, no observer is created or observed, and cleanup invokes callback with undefined.
When an observer callback receives an empty entries array, callback is invoked with undefined.
When an observer callback receives multiple entries, callback receives the last entry.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Creates IntersectionObserver with options { rootMargin: '100px' }, observes ref.current, passes entries.pop() to callback, and disconnects during cleanup.
detail.summary: Registers an intersection observer for the referenced element unless observation is unavailable or disabled. It forwards the latest intersection entry to the callback and invokes the callback with no entry when the effect is cleaned up.

specLiterals.role: IntersectionObserver rootMargin configuring the observation threshold distance.

no observer is created or observed, and callback is invoked with undefined.

detail.name: useForwardedRef
preconditions: The function is called during a valid React component or custom-hook render.
postconditions: Returns the ref object created for the hook's inner state.
If a forwarded ref is provided, React is configured to assign it through an imperative handle.
invariants: The returned inner ref object remains stable across rerenders of the same mounted hook instance.
The inner ref is initialized with a current value of null.
The imperative handle is configured with an empty dependency list.
edgeCases: When ref is omitted or undefined, the inner ref is still created and returned, but no caller-provided ref is available for forwarding.
When the inner ref's current value is null, the imperative-handle factory evaluates to null at that point.
stateMutations: React-managed current value of the inner ref.
The provided forwarded ref is assigned by React.useImperativeHandle when React applies the imperative handle.
detail.summary: Creates and returns a stable React ref object for values of type T. When a forwarded ref is provided, it exposes the inner ref's current value through React's imperative-handle mechanism.

specTests.then: It returns a ref object whose current value is initially null.

specTests.when: useForwardedRef<T>(ref) is called and React applies the imperative handle.
specTests.then: The provided ref is managed through an imperative handle whose value is the inner ref's current value.
